extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians doing research (graduate students, postdocs, faculty) interested in improving research practice and exposition
extracted.subtask_description: Recording sketches of mathematical arguments and informal notes to preserve ideas, test understanding, and develop exposition skills for later use in papers, lectures, or proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal knowledge preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: It makes the argument permanently available to you in the future, and may eventually be helpful in your later research papers, lecture notes, teaching, or research proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sketches of interesting arguments so they are permanently available later; keep them digitally with backups so incomplete or abandoned work can be retrieved and reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing provides practice with TeX, exposition, pedagogical clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regular writing to improve technical facility with TeX and to sharpen exposition and pedagogical presentation, which benefits talks, notes, and papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehension testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing forces genuine understanding. If you cannot articulate an argument coherently on paper, you haven't truly mastered it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the act of writing as a test: attempt to write the argument clearly — inability to do so indicates gaps in understanding that need repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: "It frees up mental space; you no longer have to remember the exact details of the argument, and so can devote your memory to learning newer topics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Externalize details in written sketches so you don't need to retain every technical detail mentally, allowing cognitive resources to focus on new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve incomplete or abandoned work
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve incomplete or abandoned work through informal sketches stored digitally with backups; these may prove useful later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep informal/sketchy write-ups of partial ideas or abandoned approaches, store them in backed-up digital form, since they can later inform new projects or be resurrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing as a tool of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing is not merely output but a tool of thought. A "good" math piece reflects an author who has used writing to test their own understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach writing as part of the thinking process — use it to clarify ideas and verify understanding rather than treating it only as final presentation.
